✅ Implementation: Bruno API Documentation

This document provides a highly detailed, step-by-step implementation guide to execute the exhaustive tasks outlined in API_Documentation_Task_Plan.md. It covers environment configuration, scripting, testing, and CI/CD integration based on the api-collection/Panorra API Feeds directory.

1. Initial Configuration & Environments

Before documenting individual endpoints, we must accurately map out the environments in Bruno.

1.1 Environment Setup

  1. Open Bruno and navigate to the Environments tab for the Panorra API Feeds collection.
  2. Ensure the following environments are properly configured exactly as in the environments/ folder:
    • Local - Dev (Variables: base_url = http://127.0.0.1:9999)
    • Dev (Variables: base_url = https://dev-feeds.panorra.com)
    • Live (Variables: base_url = https://feeds.panorra.com)
  3. Add a global variable token (leave the value blank initially) to store the dynamically extracted JWT/Bearer token.

1.2 Global Headers

  1. Open the Collection Settings in Bruno.
  2. Under the Headers tab, set default headers for all requests (unless overridden by specific requests):
    • Content-Type: application/json
    • Accept: application/json

1.3 Authentication Handling (Pre-request Script)

To avoid manual token entry across numerous endpoints, use Bruno's pre-request script feature at the root collection level.

  1. Open Collection Settings > Script > Pre Request.
  2. Add the following snippet:
const token = bru.getEnvVar("token");
if (token) {
  // Assuming Bearer authentication. Adjust if the API uses a different auth scheme.
  req.setHeader("Authorization", `Bearer ${token}`);
}

2. Implementing the Initial Tokens (The Foundation)

Because this project (panorra-api-go) strictly implements GET methods, mutations like Login are handled externally. However, you will need a valid token to test the feeds API.

Example: Handling Authentication for Feeds Testing

You can manually inject the token in the environment variables, or use a helper endpoint from the mutation service if provided in the collection.

  1. Method: Obtain a token from the mutation API manually.
  2. Action: Copy the JWT and paste it into the Bruno environment variable token.

Alternatively, if there is a Generate Token.yml endpoint in the Centrifugo folder or similar:

  1. Method: GET
  2. URL: {{base_url}}/auth/token...
  3. Post-response Script (Token Extraction): 
    const resData = res.getBody();
if (resData && resData.data && resData.data.token) {
  bru.setEnvVar("token", resData.data.token);
  console.log("Token successfully extracted and saved to environment!");
}

3. Implementing Core Features (User, Posts, Notification, Search)

For modules containing dozens of files and subdirectories, standardization is key.

3.1 Standard Documentation Requirements

For every endpoint in these folders, the assigned developer must complete the following checklist:

  1. Path Variables: Use Bruno variables instead of hardcoded IDs.
    • Bad: GET {{base_url}}/users/detail?id=12345
    • Good: GET {{base_url}}/users/detail?id={{user_id}} (and define user_id in the environment or request vars).
  2. Query Parameters: Document all available filters natively in the Query tab so they are visible.
    • Example: ?limit=10&page=1&include=username,avatar
  3. Save Examples: This is crucial. Once an endpoint works against Local - Dev, click Save Example in Bruno. This caches the response payload, allowing front-end devs to mock the API without running the backend.

3.2 Testing GET Feeds and Search

Many endpoints in Posts, Elastic, and Search depend heavily on query string parameters for filtering and pagination.

  1. Map out all search parameters (e.g., search, sort, page).
  2. Include at least two saved examples: one for a successful search with results (200 OK) and one for an empty state (200 OK with data: []).

4. Background Tasks (QUEUE, Support, Centrifugo)

These endpoints often have different authentication requirements or bypass standard user auth.

  1. QUEUE Endpoints: If they require a specific server-to-server secret or IP whitelisting, document this in the endpoint's Notes tab in Bruno. If a specific header is required (e.g., X-Cron-Secret), add it to the request headers.
  2. Centrifugo: Document the WebSocket token generation payload precisely in the Centrifugo folder endpoints.

5. Export and CLI Integration (CI/CD)

Once the documentation is robust and tests are written, integrate it into your automated pipelines.

  1. Install Bruno CLI globally: 
    npm install -g @usebruno/cli
  2. Run the collection locally (for testing): 
    bru run --env "Local - Dev"
  3. Generate Static HTML Documentation: 
    bru export --format html --output api-docs.html
  4. CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions Example):
    Create a workflow file .github/workflows/bruno.yml: 
    name: Run API Tests
on: [push]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      - run: npm install -g @usebruno/cli
      - run: bru run --env Dev

Exhaustive checklist for building, organizing, and maintaining the API documentation using Bruno, based on the exact contents of the api-collection/Panorra API Feeds directory.

This document describes the implementation details for the POTD broadcast list task.

Task Summary

Create a new POTD API without overwriting the original broadcast list API.

Requirements:

  • Keep ListBroadcast unchanged.
  • Add a new endpoint for POTD list data.
  • Split POTD data from the start by type=posts or type=bookmark.
  • Keep the response shape close to ListBroadcast.
  • Add location.
  • Do not add a separate coordinate field.
  • Add include filtering through Functions.GetValidIncludes.

Files Changed

File Change
src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go New action for POTD broadcast list.
src/Controllers/V1/BroadcastControllers.go Added ListPotdBroadcast controller wrapper.
src/Routes/V1/BroadcastRoutes.go Added GET /notification/list-potd.
api-collection/Panorra API Feeds/Broadcast/List POTD.yml Added Bruno API collection item.
docs/API/list-potd-broadcast-api.md Added API contract documentation.
docs/API/list-potd-broadcast-implementation.md Added implementation documentation.

Routing

Route file:

notification.Get("/list-potd", Controllers.ListPotdBroadcast)

Controller wrapper:

func ListPotdBroadcast(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
    return BroadcastAction.ListPotdBroadcast(c)
}

Query Flow

The action reads:

  • type
  • page
  • limit
  • search
  • include
  • sp
  • ec

The type query parameter is required.

Allowed values:

  • posts
  • bookmark

Invalid or missing values return:

return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 400, fiber.ErrBadRequest.Message, "Invalid type")

Include Filtering

The action supports an optional include query parameter.

Allowed fields:

allowedFields := []string{
    "broadcast_type",
    "title",
    "messages",
    "slug",
    "location",
    "post",
    "user",
    "bookmark",
}

Validation uses the existing helper:

validFields := Functions.GetValidIncludes(include, allowedFields)

The result is converted into a map for fast checks while mapping each response item:

includeMap := map[string]bool{}
for _, field := range validFields {
    includeMap[field] = true
}
shouldInclude := func(field string) bool {
    return include == "" || includeMap[field]
}

Behavior:

  • Empty include returns the full default response shape.
  • Non-empty include returns only valid requested fields.
  • Unknown fields are ignored.
  • id is denied by Functions.GetValidIncludes.
  • Bookmark count and thumbnail lookup only run when bookmark is included, reducing unnecessary DB work.

Bookmark Query

When type=bookmark, the query joins only the bookmark-related tables:

  • broadcast b
  • folder_bookmark fb
  • users u

Main filters:

  • b.post_type = 'bookmark'
  • b.folder_id IS NOT NULL
  • fb.is_published = true

Owner data comes from:

u.id = fb.user_id

Location source:

fb.location

Search checks:

  • b.messages
  • b.title
  • b.slug
  • fb.name

Posts Query

When type=posts, the query joins only the post-related tables:

  • broadcast b
  • posts p
  • users u

Main filters:

  • b.post_type = 'post'
  • b.post_id IS NOT NULL

Owner data comes from:

u.id = p.user_id

Location source:

p.location_post AS location

Search checks:

  • b.messages
  • b.title
  • b.slug
  • p.description

Shared Behavior

Both types reuse the same behavior as ListBroadcast where applicable:

  • Auth check with UserFunctions.UserDatas.
  • Support account check with sp=true.
  • Deactivated user filtering from Redis key PREFIX_deactive_users_ec.
  • Blocked user filtering from Redis key PREFIX_blocked_users_ec_<encrypt>.
  • Pagination through page, limit, and offset.
  • HTML unescape for title and messages.
  • JSON unmarshal for JSON fields such as location, panorama_quality, and filters.
  • Optional encrypted response when request header ec is true.

Response Mapping

The response envelope remains:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "List POTD Broadcast",
    "broadcast": []
  }
}

For type=bookmark, each item includes:

  • broadcast_type
  • title
  • messages
  • slug
  • location
  • bookmark

For type=posts, each item includes:

  • broadcast_type
  • title
  • messages
  • slug
  • location
  • post
  • user

When include is present, the item is filtered after all required parsing and shaping:

GET /notification/list-potd?type=bookmark&include=title,location,bookmark

Response item:

{
  "title": "Holiday Places",
  "location": {
    "lat": -8.409518,
    "lng": 115.188919
  },
  "bookmark": {
    "total": 5,
    "thumbnail": "sample.jpg",
    "name": "Holiday Places"
  }
}

Why Joins Are Split By Type

The first implementation used shared joins for both post and bookmark paths. The query was then updated to split joins by type.

Reason:

  • Avoid joining unused tables.
  • Make the SQL easier to read.
  • Keep search conditions aligned with the selected type.
  • Prevent bookmark-only filters from affecting post results, and post-only search from affecting bookmark results.

Verification

Compile and package verification:

go test ./...

Expected result:

?    panorra-api-go/src/Action/V1/Broadcast    [no test files]
...

The latest run completed successfully with exit code 0.

Description

  • Add params type posts/bookmark.
  • Item add object: coordinate ([lat, long]), location.

Design notes (from brainstorm 2026-07-08)

Decision: two separate endpoints (not one unified type handler). type = posts | bookmark is the frontend tab selector that picks which endpoint to call.

A1 — Posts tab: extend most-popular-post (/v1/posts/most-popular-post, -feed, sl/ twins)

  • Add location_post, location_name to the views_timeline_post select (feed variant currently omits location_post).
  • Each item gains location (from location_name) and coordinate parsed from location_post JSONB (latitude/longitude). coordinate = null when the post has no location; map skips nulls.

A2 — Bookmarks tab: new list endpoint (e.g. GET /v1/posts/potd-bookmark)

  • Support-published folder = a row in the broadcast table with that folder_id (existing pattern, no new column).
  • Returns the existing folder-card shape (name, slug, thumbnails[4], total-bookmark counter, potd, is_published) plus location + coordinate.
  • Apply the standard blocked-user / blocked-post / deactivated-user filters.

Open questions

  1. Coordinate as object {lat,lng} (recommended) vs array [lat, long] as written above?
  2. Folder map coordinate: one representative point (recommended v1) vs array of the folder's post pins?
  3. Endpoint naming/path (potd-bookmark under posts/ or broadcast/?).
  4. Do the bookmark cards need the slim (sl/) + ec encrypted variants?
  5. Role: allow viewer for the bookmark list, or user only?

✅ Implementation: DetailBroadcastPost Location Fields

Overview

This document outlines the implementation details for updating the DetailBroadcastPost API endpoint to include location_name and location_post inside the returned post object.

File Modified

  • src/Action/V1/Broadcast/DetailBroadcastPost.go

Technical Details

The endpoint builds the broadcast detail response from a manual GORM query against the posts, broadcast, and users tables.

The update is additive and keeps the existing response structure intact. The new location fields are returned under broadcast.post, because the location data belongs to the post being broadcast.

Query Update

The select clause now retrieves the post location fields from the posts table:

 Select(`
 	b.messages, b.title, b.post_type as broadcast_type,
 	p.slug as slug_post, p.panorama_preview, p.thumbnail, p.post_type,
+	p.location_name, p.location_post,
 	u.username, u.fullname, u.avatar
 `)

The post object now includes location_name and location_post:

 post := map[string]interface{}{
 	"slug_post":        broadcast["slug_post"],
 	"panorama_preview": broadcast["panorama_preview"],
 	"post_type":        broadcast["post_type"],
 	"thumbnail":        broadcast["thumbnail"],
+	"location_name":    broadcast["location_name"],
+	"location_post":    broadcast["location_post"],
 }

Response Impact

Before this update, broadcast.post only returned post identity and media preview fields.

After this update, broadcast.post also returns:

{
  "location_name": "Location name value",
  "location_post": {
    "latitude": "0.000000",
    "longitude": "0.000000"
  }
}

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 07/07/26

✅ Implementation: API Search Folder Bookmark Published

Example Search Published Folder Bookmark API

Endpoint: GET /search/folder-bookmark/published
Description: Retrieves a list of publicly published folder bookmarks from all creators. This endpoint powers the Bookmark tab in the Search Discover page, providing infinite scroll capabilities, full-text search, and category filtering.

Example cURL Request

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/search/folder-bookmark/published" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  --data-urlencode "page=1" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10" \
  --data-urlencode "q=holiday" \
  --data-urlencode "category=0" \
  --data-urlencode "include=slug,name,thumbnail,user,total_bookmark"

Request Parameters

  • page (int, optional): Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1.
  • limit (int, optional): Number of items per page. Defaults to 8.
  • q (string, optional): Keyword to search published folders by name. (Also supports name as an alias for backward compatibility).
  • category (int, optional): Filter by category_id. Passing 0 or omitting it skips the category filter.
  • include (string, optional): Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response (e.g., slug,name,user). Using this limits the output only to the specified fields.
  • include (allowed): ("slug", "name", "description", "location", "location_name", "category_name", "published_at", "total_bookmark", "thumbnail", "user", "potd")

Success Response

The response includes the folder details along with nested user, geo location, and a strictly formatted total_bookmark object.

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "Search Published Folder Bookmarks",
    "bookmarks": [
      {
        "slug": "holiday-places-2024",
        "name": "Holiday Places",
        "description": "Places to visit",
        "location": {
            "lat": -8.409518, 
            "lng": 115.188919
        },
        "location_name": "Bali",
        "category_name": "Leisure",
        "published_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "potd": false,
        "total_bookmark": {
            "counter_bookmak": 5
        },
        "thumbnail": "sample.jpg",
        "user": {
            "username": "tester",
            "avatar": "avatar.jpg",
            "encrypt": "abcd123"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Error Responses

Unauthorized (User context invalid or missing):

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "data": {
    "error": "Unauthorized"
  }
}

Internal Server Error (Database connection failure):

{
  "statusCode": 500,
  "data": {
    "error": "Internal Server Error"
  }
}

Overview

This implementation addresses Github Task #450 ("Update API Search Bookmark") by creating a dedicated endpoint rather than modifying the existing SearchFolderBookmark logic. This ensures that the current user's bookmark searching logic remains intact while providing the Frontend with a specialized endpoint for the "Search Discover" page to query publicly published bookmarks globally.

Files Created/Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPublishedFolderBookmark.go (New File)
  2. src/Controllers/V1/SearchControllers.go (Modified)
  3. src/Routes/V1/SearchRoutes.go (Modified)
  4. src/Models/SearchModel.go (Modified - Added SearchFolderBookmark struct)

Technical Details

1. New Endpoint Route

  • Path: GET /search/published-folder-bookmark
  • Controller: SearchPublishedFolderBookmark

2. Querying Strategy

Instead of querying the base folder_bookmark table filtered by the current user (user_id = ?), the new logic queries the views_published_folders PostgreSQL view. This satisfies the requirement to "Discover publicly published bookmarks from all creators".

3. Filters and Parameters Supported

  • q (and name as fallback): Used to perform an ILIKE search against the folder name.
  • category: When provided (and not 0), filters the folders strictly to the requested category_id.
  • page & limit: Used to paginate results for infinite scrolling on the frontend.
  • Implicitly orders by published_at DESC for a "recent list" output when query params are empty.

4. Struct and Response Formatting

A new struct SearchFolderBookmark was added to Models/SearchModel.go. It facilitates mapping the flat structure of the views_published_folders view into the nested JSON objects required by the frontend:

  • Owner Mapping: owner_username, owner_avatar, and owner_encrypt are grouped into a user JSON payload.
  • Geo-Location: The location JSONB field is passed directly to the response to support map markers.
  • Bookmark Count: The total_bookmark integer from the view is re-formatted in code to a JSON object ({"counter_bookmak": <value>}) to strictly match legacy formatting without needing to trigger extra ElasticSearch queries during the loop.

Security Considerations

Blocked users, deactivated users, and the requester's own privacy settings (e.g. blockUser, deactiveUser) are still respected by actively filtering out folders where owner_encrypt IN (?).

RESULT 15/07/26

✅ Implementation: Create views_published_folder_posts And Indexes Implementation

Summary

Prepared the DB view and indexes needed by GET /bookmark/published/:slug. The view uses views_timeline_post_slim as the counter source because its aggregate JSON is already available in the database and has known shape.

View Name

public.views_published_folder_posts

Counter Source

views_timeline_post_slim exposes:

views_aggregate = {"aggregate": {"count": 48}}
comments_aggregate = {"aggregate": {"count": 21}}
likes_aggregate = {"aggregate": {"count": 3}, "nodes": []}

The new view extracts integer counters:

  • counter_view
  • counter_like
  • counter_comment

View DDL

Run the full statement, from CREATE through ;.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.views_published_folder_posts AS
SELECT
    fb.id AS folder_id,
    fb.slug AS folder_slug,
    b.created_at AS bookmark_created_at,
    vts.id AS post_id,
    vts.slug AS slug,
    vts.description AS description,
    vts.thumbnail AS thumbnail,
    vts.post_type AS post_type,
    vts.visibility AS visibility,
    true AS is_publish,
    vts.data_user::jsonb #>> '{encrypt}' AS encrypt,
    vts.data_user::jsonb #>> '{username}' AS username,
    vts.data_user::jsonb #>> '{avatar}' AS avatar,
    CASE
        WHEN br_folder.folder_id IS NOT NULL OR vts.potd = true THEN true
        ELSE false
    END AS potd,
    CAST(COALESCE(vts.views_aggregate::jsonb #>> '{aggregate,count}', '0') AS bigint) AS counter_view,
    CAST(COALESCE(vts.likes_aggregate::jsonb #>> '{aggregate,count}', '0') AS bigint) AS counter_like,
    CAST(COALESCE(vts.comments_aggregate::jsonb #>> '{aggregate,count}', '0') AS bigint) AS counter_comment
FROM public.bookmark AS b
JOIN public.folder_bookmark AS fb ON fb.id = b.folder_id
JOIN public.views_timeline_post_slim AS vts ON vts.id = b.post_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT folder_id
    FROM public.broadcast
    WHERE folder_id IS NOT NULL
) AS br_folder ON br_folder.folder_id = fb.id
WHERE fb.is_published = true;

Index DDL

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_folder_bookmark_published_slug
ON public.folder_bookmark (slug)
WHERE is_published = true;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bookmark_folder_created_at
ON public.bookmark (folder_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bookmark_post_id
ON public.bookmark (post_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_broadcast_folder_id
ON public.broadcast (folder_id)
WHERE folder_id IS NOT NULL;

Optional, only if these do not already exist:

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_posts_publish_banned_user_id
ON public.posts (is_publish, banned, user_id, id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_id_banned
ON public.users (id, banned);

API Query Shape

The API reads:

SELECT
    slug,
    username,
    avatar,
    description,
    thumbnail,
    post_type,
    potd,
    counter_view,
    counter_like,
    counter_comment
FROM public.views_published_folder_posts
WHERE folder_slug = $1
  AND visibility = 'public'
  AND is_publish = true
  AND post_type != 'video360'
ORDER BY bookmark_created_at DESC
LIMIT $2
OFFSET $3;

For total_posts:

SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM public.views_published_folder_posts
WHERE folder_slug = $1
  AND visibility = 'public'
  AND is_publish = true
  AND post_type != 'video360';

For total_views_all_posts:

SELECT COALESCE(SUM(counter_view), 0)
FROM public.views_published_folder_posts
WHERE folder_slug = $1
  AND visibility = 'public'
  AND is_publish = true
  AND post_type != 'video360';
